input: Sign up for a local volunteer cleanup event

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The user's city or neighborhood determines which specific events and organizations are actually available to them.
Cleanup events vary widely — parks, beaches, rivers, streets, etc. — and the user may have a specific environment in mind, which narrows the search.
Knowing which dates or days of the week the user is available rules out events that don't fit their schedule before wasting time researching them.
Whether the user is signing up solo, with friends, or as a group (e.g., family with kids) affects which events are suitable and how many spots need to be reserved.
The user may prefer a one-time event vs. an ongoing commitment, or a large organized event vs. a small community gathering — this shapes which options to prioritize.
Understanding whether the user already has a specific organization or event in mind vs. needing to discover options determines the very first action to take.
Some users just want to show up once; others want to build a volunteer habit or earn hours for a requirement — knowing this shapes how thoroughly to vet the event.

gold.taskTitle: Sign up for a local volunteer cleanup event
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find and register for a volunteer cleanup event happening in their local area.

questions.title: What city or neighborhood are you based in?
questions.description: The user's location is essential for finding relevant local cleanup events and organizations.

questions.title: What type of environment do you want to clean up?
questions.description: Identifying a preferred setting — park, beach, river, urban streets, trails — narrows the search to matching events.

questions.title: Which dates or days of the week are you available?
questions.description: Availability constraints immediately filter out events the user cannot attend, making the search more efficient.

questions.title: Are you signing up alone, or bringing others with you?
questions.description: Knowing whether this is a solo signup or a group (friends, family, children) affects which events are appropriate and how many registrations are needed.

questions.title: Do you want a one-time event or a recurring commitment?
questions.description: Some users want a single Saturday event; others want to join an ongoing volunteer program — this shapes which options to surface.

questions.title: Do you already have an organization or event in mind?
questions.description: If the user already knows of a specific group or event, the task is registration only; if not, discovery is the first step.

questions.title: Do you need to log volunteer hours for any requirement?
questions.description: If the user needs certified hours for school, work, or court, the event must offer official verification — a key filter for choosing the right one.
